rules.status_cite: p. 74: "OPINION AND ORDER ... Entered in the Journal on July 9, 2025" | p. 170, VII. Order, para. 171: "ORDERED, That the 10/23 Stipulation be approved and adopted, subject to modifications consistent with this Order."

threshold_mw.v: 25 MW: Schedule DCT applies to data center ESAs signed after the effective date for new load or expansion greater in the aggregate than 25 MW
threshold_mw.cite: p. 89, Summary of the Stipulations, 10/23 Stipulation, Tariff Applicability: "Schedule Data Center Tariff (DCT) would apply to any data center customer ESA signed after the tariff effective date for a" | p. 90, Summary of the Stipulations, 10/23 Stipulation, Tariff Applicability: "new load (or expansion of an existing load) greater in the aggregate than 25 MW." | p. 94, Aggregation: "If there are multiple new facilities at a single location of less than 25 MW, but the aggregate total load is greater than 25 MW, all of those facilities will be subject to Schedule DCT."

min_demand.v: Greater of 85 percent of the highest billing demand of the past 11 months or the contract-capacity schedule (25,001 to 75,000 kW: 15,000 kW plus 85 percent above 25,000 kW; over 75,000 kW: 57,500 kW plus 100 percent above 75,000 kW), capped at 85 percent of total contract capacity; ramp floors 50, 65, 80 and 90 percent in years 1 to 4
min_demand.cite: p. 92, Minimum Demand Charges, 10/23 Stipulation: "a) 85-percent of the customer's highest previously established monthly billing demand during the past 11 months; or" | p. 92, Minimum Demand Charges, 10/23 Stipulation: "for customers with 25,001 kW to 75,000 kW of total contract capacity: minimum demand is 15,000 kW plus 85 percent of any capacity above 25,000 kW; or with more than 75,000 kW of total contract capacity, minimum demand is 57,500 kW plus 100 percent of any capacity above 75,000 kW. However, the minimum demand cannot exceed 85 percent of the total contract capacity." | p. 91, Load Ramp Period, 10/23 Stipulation: "In Year 1: 50-percent contract capacity In Year 2: 65-percent contract capacity In Year 3: 80-percent contract capacity In Year 4: 90-percent contract capacity"

contract_term.v: Initial term equal to the Load Ramp Period (no greater than four years) plus eight years
contract_term.cite: p. 91, Contract Term, 10/23 Stipulation: "The initial term of the contract will equal the Load Ramp Period (no greater than four years) plus eight years."

collateral.v: For customers below A-/A3 ratings, a parent guarantee or collateral (letter of credit or cash) equal to 50 percent of the customer's minimum charges under the ESA; the Commission's modification lets the customer's financial sponsor meet it as a co-signer
collateral.cite: p. 91, Collateral, 10/23 Stipulation: "Collateral and other tariff requirements will remain the same, as requested in the Company's application (which would require data center customers who have credit ratings less than A- from S&P, A3 from Moody's to provide a parent guarantee or collateral in the form of a letter of credit or cash equal to 50 percent of the customer's minimum charges under the ESA." | p. 150: "We find that, the collateral requirements must either be met by the data center customer or the customer's financial sponsor, so long as the sponsor is a co-signer on the contract with AEP Ohio."

exit_fee.v: Exit fee payable only after five contract years excluding the load ramp period (with a three-year ramp, after year eight); exit fee and collateral revenue to flow back to retail customers
exit_fee.cite: p. 96, Exit Fees, 10/23 Stipulation: "Data centers will be eligible to pay the applicable exit fee after the completion of five years of the contract, excluding load ramp period, meaning if there is a load ramp period of three years, the customer may exit after year eight (three year load ramp period and five years of contract)."

study_timeline.v: Load study fee of $10k to $100k paid within 45 days; reasonable efforts to complete the load study within 60 days if regional transmission upgrades are needed, otherwise 45 days; 60 days to sign the LOA and ESA
study_timeline.cite: p. 94, Signing Up New Customers, 10/23 Stipulation: "AEP Ohio will charge a one-time fee for each load study from $10k to $100k to be paid within 45 days or customers will forfeit their spot." | p. 95, Signing Up New Customers, 10/23 Stipulation: "will make reasonable efforts to complete a load study within (i) 60 days if regional transmission upgrades are needed to serve the customer; or (ii) 45 days (for all other situations)." | p. 95, Signing Up New Customers, 10/23 Stipulation: "4) Customer will have 60 days to sign the LOA and ESA."

min_demand.v: Monthly billing demand not less than 90% of the greater of on-peak contract capacity, the highest billing demand of the past 11 months, or the month's maximum demand
min_demand.cite: p. 63, Sheet 8-3: "the customer’s monthly billing demand shall in no event be less than 90% of the greater of (a) the customer's on-peak contract capacity or b) the customer’s highest previously established monthly billing demand during the past 11 months or (c) the customer’s maximum demand created during the billing month."

contract_term.v: Initial period of 20 years; at least five years' written notice to discontinue (not reducing the 20-year term); five years' notice to reduce contract capacity, by no more than 20% except by mutual agreement, not given in the first five years
contract_term.cite: p. 63, Sheet 8-3: "Contracts will be made for an initial period of twenty (20) years and shall remain in effect thereafter unless cancelled or modified pursuant to the terms hereunder." | p. 63, Sheet 8-3: "Either party shall give at least five years’ written notice to the other of the intention to discontinue service under the terms of this Schedule. collateral.v: 24 times the previous maximum monthly non-fuel bill (the maximum expected bill in the first contract year), recomputed annually and updated if 10% greater

exit_fee.cite: p. 63, Sheet 8-3: "In the event of a permanent closure by the customer occurring after the first five (5) years of the initial contract term, the customer may exit the contract by providing a one-time payment equal to five (5) years of minimum billing under this Schedule."

contract_term.cite: searched: Sheets R-21 and R-54 (EFIS 865322 pp. 39 and 40): a Letter of Agreement is required but no term is printed.

collateral.v: A refundable deposit of $200,000 with the Letter of Agreement, to offset project planning costs; if costs exceed it, an additional refundable deposit of $200,000; further refundable deposits (no amount stated) so that the customer pays all project planning costs; unused initial deposit funds refunded without interest; projects the Company designates as serving the community interest may be prioritized and may not be required to submit a deposit; substation or transmission extensions are paid in full by the customer (SPP network upgrades excluded)
collateral.cite: p. 39: "submit a refundable deposit of $200,000 that will be used to offset costs associated with project planning." | p. 39: "Should costs exceed this deposit an additional refundable deposit of $200,000 shall be required." | p. 39: "Additional refundable deposits will be required such that the Customer pays all project planning costs associated with their project." | p. 39: "Initial deposit funds not used during planning shall be refunded to the customer without interest." | p. 39: "may be given priority in the queue and may not be required to submit a deposit" | p. 40, Sheet R-54, 7.11 E: "any Customer requesting service with substation or transmission facilities shall pay all costs associated with such extensions. These costs do not include any resulting Network Upgrade costs for facilities classified as transmission under the Southwest Power Pool Open Access Transmission Tariff."

exit_fee.cite: searched: Sheets R-21 and R-54 (EFIS 865322 pp. 39 and 40): no exit or termination charge.

study_timeline.v: No study duration published. Customers are queued by the date they gave the required information and deposit; the Company works on advanced study and scoping for up to four projects at a time; once an Initial Projects Agreement is complete the details go to SPP for review; completed plans are valid for six months
study_timeline.cite: p. 39, Sheet R-21, 2.10 B: "These Customers shall be placed in a queue based on the date on which they provided the required information and deposit." | p. 39, Sheet R-21, 2.10 C: "The Company will work on advanced study and scoping for up to four (4) projects at a time." | p. 39, Sheet R-21, 2.10 C: "Once an Initial Projects Agreement is complete, the Company will send necessary details to the Southwest Power Pool ("SPP") for its review. Completed plans shall be valid for six months."

connection_timeline.v: No time to energize published. Construction of a substation or transmission extension begins only after the customer completes payment or arranges installments and executes the extension agreements and any Service Agreements the rate schedule requires; customers failing to complete the agreements within the timeframe allowed may be returned to the queue (no timeframe printed)
connection_timeline.cite: p. 40, Sheet R-54, 7.11 E: "Customers requesting service through substation or transmission facilities must complete payment for the extension or make suitable arrangements for installment payments, execute all required agreements associated with the requested extensions, and execute any Service Agreements required by the applicable rate schedule as a condition for any construction to commence." | p. 39, Sheet R-21, 2.10 D: "Customers failing to complete these agreements within the timeframe allowed may be returned to the queue."

rules.docket_cite: p. 16: "the Commission reviewed Evergy's Large Load Power Service (LLPS) tariff, in Docket No. 25-EKME-315-TAR."

threshold_mw.v: 75 MW: a new customer with a peak load of 75 MW or greater, or an existing customer expanding by 75 MW or greater
threshold_mw.cite: p. 16: "The rate would apply to any new customer with a peak load of 75 MW or greater, or an existing customer with an expansion of 75 MW or greater." | https://www.kcc.ks.gov/news-11-6-25 (read 2026-11-13) KCC news release of 6 November 2025: "The new LLPS rates will apply to any new facility beginning service with a peak load forecast at 75 megawatts (75 MW) or more, or an existing customer expecting to expand by 75 MW."

min_demand.v: Minimum monthly bill based on 80 percent of contract demand, whatever the actual usage
min_demand.cite: p. 17: "Customers pay a minimum monthly bill that is based on 80% of their contract demand, regardless of their actual monthly usage."

contract_term.v: 12 years plus an optional load ramp of up to five years (up to 17 years in all); then automatic five-year extensions
contract_term.cite: p. 16: "Customers will be required to sign a 12-year contract, plus an optional load ramp period of up to five years, for a total contract length of up to" | p. 17: "17-years. Thereafter, the contract automatically extends for five years at a time."

collateral.v: Two years of Minimum Monthly Bills, as calculated by Evergy, under creditworthiness standards
collateral.cite: p. 17: "Schedule LLPS customers are required to provide collateral in an amount equal to two (2) years of Minimum Monthly Bills, as calculated by Evergy." | https://www.kcc.ks.gov/images/PDFs/presentations-and-legislative-testimony/2026_Senate%20Utilities%20Committee%20Update_15Jan.pdf (read 2026-11-13) p. 11, KCC Utilities Division slides, 15 January 2026: "Collateral requirements of up to 2 years of Minimum Bills."

exit_fee.v: 36 months' advance notice to terminate early, and an exit fee of the Minimum Monthly Bill times the months remaining in the term, or 12 months, whichever is greater; with less than 36 months' notice, the exit fee plus two times the Minimum Monthly Bill times the months short of 36. Capacity may be reduced by the lower of 25 MW or 10 percent of contract capacity
exit_fee.cite: p. 17: "If the customer terminates service early, they are required to provide 36-months advance notice, and pay an exit fee equal to the nominal value of the minimum monthly bill times the number of months remaining in the contract term, or 12-months, whichever is greater." | p. 17: "the Exit Fee plus two (2) times the nominal value of the Minimum Monthly Bill times the number of months less than the thirty-six (36) months' notice required for termination." | p. 17: "Customers taking LLPS service can reduce their service under the tariff rate by 25 MW or up to 10 percent of the total capacity of the contract, whichever is lower."

rules.clause: p. 16, Evergy Kansas Metro and Evergy Kansas Central, LLPS Tariff Docket (25-315 Docket): "A new tariffed offering called the LLPS rate."
rules.basis: the Kansas Corporation Commission's own report, slides and news release on kcc.ks.gov; the queue figure from Evergy's filings on SEC EDGAR
rules.notes: Rates (KCC report p. 17, from the settlement): Evergy Kansas Central LLPS customer charge $386.67 per month, demand charges $22.985/kW summer and $20.817/kW winter, energy $0.00872/kWh, Grid charges $0.248/kW substation and $0.156/kW transmission; Evergy Kansas Metro customer charge $751.02, demand $21.174/kW summer and $19.174/kW winter, energy $0.01000/kWh, Grid $0.200/kW substation and $0.126/kW transmission (for the ERW's registry's tariff table, not one of this row's fields). The application of 11 February 2025 proposed the rate for customers over 100 MW (report p. 16); the settlement lowered it to 75 MW. Settlement filed 18 August 2025, hearing 8 October 2025 (slides p. 8). The slides (p. 18) say LLPS applies only in the Evergy Kansas Central and Evergy Kansas Metro service territories (Evergy Kansas South lies within Evergy Kansas Central's). The tariff's effective date was not read in a primary document (CURB's newsletter, another party, is a lead only), so the status is approved with the order date. Evergy 10-Q table: remaining contractual minimum consideration for large load contracts $8.9 billion (Evergy), weighted average remaining term 15 years, as of 30 September 2026. Refused: the KCC order on kcc-connect.kcc.ks.gov (bot check); evergy.com not requested. Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-35): the 10-Q was described as 'filed 5 November 2026', which it does not print; it is dated 4 November 2026.

rules.basis: the City of Seattle's legislative record (seattle.legistar.com) and City web pages; seattle.gov's terms of use (https://www.seattle.gov/digital/terms-of-use, read 13 November 2026) set no limit on use or reproduction
rules.notes: Status: passed by the City Council on 21 July 2026 and signed by the Mayor on 22 July 2026 (the legislation history); City Light says the policy took effect immediately; the class covers capacity installed after 1 January 2027 (the definition) The signed Ordinance 127473 PDF (legistar2.granicus.com) is refused by robots; the text read is the passed version 2 of the bill on seattle.legistar.com (the history shows version 2 passed by the Council on 21 July 2026 after the committee's amendment of 15 July). Other conditions of SMC 21.49.059: curtailment provisions and energy conservation measures (B.5, B.6), full recovery of the procurement cost of new resources (B.8), energy and demand charges at City Light's marginal cost plus a service fee (D.1). City Light's own summary: threshold "10 megavolt-amperes (MVA) or more" (post); the Review Panel minutes of 17 June 2026 (p. 2) say "greater than 10 MVA". Separately, the City Council's one-year moratorium (Council Bill 121214) bars siting data centers over 20 MVA within city limits; that is a land-use rule, not a connection rule. Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-07): was 'in effect 2026-07'. The City Council passed the ordinance on 21 July 2026 (Legistar history). City Light's post says the policy was 'adopted, and effective immediately' in July 2026, but the ordinance's Section 15 sets its effect by SMC 1.04.020 and 1.04.070, whose dates are not printed in the copies read, and the class reaches only capacity installed after 1 January 2027.

rules.title: Virginia SCC Final Order of 25 November 2025 in Case No. PUR-2025-00058 (Doc. Con. Cen. No. 251140150), reproduced as Exhibit A to White Springs and Nucor's motion for official recognition, Florida PSC Docket No. 20260064-EI, Document No. 05289-2026, filed 18 August 2026
rules.clause: p. 31, Rate Schedule GS-5: "The Company shall implement a new rate schedule, Rate Schedule GS-5, as set forth below, effective January 1, 2027."
rules.basis: the Florida PSC's docket copy of the Virginia SCC's Final Order (the SCC's own host is paused for the ERW); the queue figures from a Dominion document PJM posts and a Dominion presentation ESIG posts; Dominion's SEC filings
rules.notes: Status: approved by the Final Order of 25 November 2025, effective 1 January 2027; Dominion's Q3 2026 10-Q says an appeal of the order to the Supreme Court of Virginia, filed March 2026, is pending. The order (PDF p. 36, ordering paragraph 4) requires the tariffs and terms and conditions effective 1 January 2027 to be filed at least 45 days before that date; that compliance filing was not read (the SCC host is paused; Dominion's own site is barred, below). The order (p. 35) also lets existing customers who would be subject to the 'High Load Customer Terms and Conditions' make a one-time downward adjustment of contracted demand without penalty before the effective date, and (p. 33, footnote 101) approves exemptions from minimum demand obligations for necessary and planned maintenance in the Terms and Conditions. Dominion's answers to Spotsylvania County (p. 1) say the contractual provisions apply, with limited exceptions, to all customers of 25 MW or more, not only GS-5. rules.basis: the session law on the New Jersey Legislature's site (pub.njleg.gov, robots allow it) and the BPU's own notice and stakeholder slides (nj.gov/bpu, robots allow it)
rules.notes: Status: The statute is in effect. The BPU's standards order (due within 12 months of enactment) and each utility's tariff petition (due within 180 days of that order) are not yet issued or filed; BPU Staff's Request for Information took responses to 13 November 2026. A statewide rule binding each New Jersey electric public utility's future large data center tariff (the Maryland and Pennsylvania model rows are alike). The enacted text is Section 1 as numbered 31 in the Fourth Reprint; the bracketed, deleted Section 1 of earlier reprints (100 MW, 85 percent for not less than 10 years) is not the law and is not quoted. Existing service: a large data center approved by a utility before the act's effective date is exempt from paragraphs (1), (2) and (8) of subsection d (the 85 percent guarantee, the security, the study costs) for the approved megawatts only (Section 1g). Other required tariff terms: demand flexibility commitments, priority curtailment before residential customers in system emergencies, disclosure of similar requests pending at other utilities (Section 1b(11) and (12), 1d(5)). BPU stakeholder meeting held 4 November 2026 (the slides). Queue: PSE&G's pipeline is on its own row; no Jersey Central Power & Light, Atlantic City Electric or Rockland Electric pipeline was found in the documents read (FirstEnergy's site terms bar reuse, siting-gaps; Exelon's terms bar automated access, pjm_east group; neither read). study_timeline.v: current practice: NYISO-jurisdictional projects, System Impact Study about 6 to 12 months and Facility Study about 6 to 15 months for lower-complexity projects; projects in a utility's local jurisdiction, capacity study then load study, generally 1 to 6 months overall

connection_timeline.v: current practice: about 42 to 80 months from initial engagement to energization, by project complexity

From the docket's listing (not cited): initial comments 13 May 2026 and replies 15 June 2026 (comment dates extended by notice of 23 March 2026); a draft scope for a Generic Environmental Impact Statement on data centers and large loads adopted 17 to 18 September 2026; a technical conference on 28 October 2026. Con Edison is read only from the DPS's copies.

Standard LEUF Agreements carry (1) a Reservation Charge based on Contract Demand, paid monthly over the term and set to recover the full cost of the generation, storage and network facilities needed to serve the load, or, where the customer chooses its own resources, direct reimbursement plus a Portfolio Risk Management Charge based on Contract Demand and a System Firming and Balancing Charge at 33 percent of Schedule 48 System Fixed Generation; (2) a Peak Demand Charge at the OATT Schedule 1, Schedule 3 and NITS rates on the month's highest demand; (3) the Schedule 300 Excess Demand Charge

contract_term.cite: p. 12, IV.H Contract term and renewals: "Paragraph 24 of the stipulation sets a minimum 10-year LEUF Agreement term, with a maximum term of 30 years, inclusive of any ramp period. Paragraph 31 provides that LEUF Agreement renewals will be at least 10 years in length."

collateral.v: At the company's election, sufficient creditworthiness or posted collateral to cover the customer's Exit Fee; creditworthiness means senior unsecured long-term debt rated A- or higher (S&P or Fitch), A (low) or higher (DBRS) or A3 or higher (Moody's), or an equivalent internal rating; the amount is reassessed every two years. Network Upgrades needed for the load are paid up front by the LEUF, except Qualified Network Upgrades (230 kV and above, on the WECC critical path list, with less than 80 percent of known capacity needs from LEUFs), which are paid as a monthly fee on the LEUF's share
collateral.cite: p. 13, IV.L Collateral and credit requirements: "Paragraph 29 of the stipulation provides that a LEUF shall, at the company's election, be required to provide sufficient creditworthiness or post collateral to cover the customer's Exit Fee." | p. 13, IV.L: "The senior unsecured long term debt of a customer has a rating of A- or higher by Standard & Poor's or Fitch, A (low) or higher by DBRS, or A3 or higher by Moody's Investor Services, Inc." | p. 13, IV.L: "The stipulation states that the amount will be reassessed every two years to reflect the customer's current Exit Fee." | p. 7, IV.E.1 Line extension and network upgrade costs: "any Network Upgrades (as defined in Rule 13, including bulk transmission) required to serve the New LEUF's load will be paid for upfront by the New LEUF"

exit_fee.v: Exit Fee set to recover company-funded infrastructure: net book value of company-funded infrastructure, net cost of customer-specific power or tolling agreements, the Reservation Charge for the remainder of the contract, and the net cost of removing facilities no longer needed; refunded pro rata if another large customer takes the capacity within three years (the removal cost is not refunded)

Engineering studies are funded separately by the LEUF

threshold_mw.v: 50,000 kVA of Reserved Capacity: new applicants signing after 25 April 2025 for total Reserved Capacity of 50,000 kVA or more, or existing customers adding 50,000 kVA above their 25 April 2025 Reserved Capacity. Customers requiring 200,000 kVA or more total load must take a special pricing contract
threshold_mw.cite: p. 271, 3(f): "(1) New Applicants that sign agreements with the Company after April 25, 2025, for total Reserved Capacity of 50,000 kVA or greater." | p. 271, 3(f): "(2) Existing Customers that sign agreements with the Company for 50,000 kVA of Reserved Capacity above and beyond the Customer's Reserved Capacity as of April 25, 2025." | p. 262, 1(h) Extension Limits: "Customers requiring 200,000 kVA or more, total load, shall enter into special pricing contracts with the Company."

min_demand.v: Minimum On-Peak Power Charge: monthly On-Peak Power billed at the higher of actual On-Peak Power usage or 75 percent of Reserved Capacity for the month; Excess Power Charge on usage above Reserved Capacity, priced as in Schedule 31; with a load ramp, both apply from the year Reserved Capacity reaches 50,000 kVA; both may be waived or modified by special contract
min_demand.cite: p. 262, 1(k) Minimum On-Peak Power Charge: "Monthly On-Peak Power charges for Very Large New Load Customers shall be billed as the highest of:" | p. 262, 1(k): "(2) Seventy-five percent (75%) of the Reserved Capacity for the applicable month." | p. 261, 1(d) Excess Power Charge: "The Excess Power Charge shall be priced consistent with the Excess Power Charge in Schedule 31 and applied to monthly power usage in excess of Reserved Capacity." | p. 271, 3(f): "For Customers with a load ramp, the Minimum On-Peak Power Charge and Excess Power Charge shall apply the year that the Customer's Reserved Capacity reaches 50,000 kVA."

contract_term.v: Minimum five years in addition to the specified load ramp period; Reserved Capacity may be reduced by up to 10 percent or 50,000 kVA a year, whichever is smaller, or more by mutual agreement
contract_term.cite: p. 271, 3(f): "Very Large New Load Customers are required to enter into contracts with a minimum term of five (5) years in addition to the specified load ramp period." | p. 271, 3(f): "Very Large New Load Customers may reduce Reserved Capacity by up to 10 percent or 50,000 kVA per year, whichever is smaller, or by an amount mutually agreed upon by the Company and the customer."

collateral.v: Sufficient credit, or posted collateral at the Company's election, to cover the Minimum On-Peak Power Charge for at least five years
collateral.cite: p. 271, 3(f): "Very Large New Load Customers are required to have sufficient credit or post collateral, at the Company's election, to cover the Minimum On-Peak Power Charge for at least five years."

rules.notes: A statewide rule, like the ERW's registry's Pennsylvania model: it binds each Maryland electric company's own large load tariff. Status: published as proposed on 26 June 2026 with comments to 27 July 2026; whether the PSC has since adopted it was not verified (a later Maryland Register issue would show the final action). Each investor-owned company had to file its own large load rate schedule by 1 September 2026: Chapter 353 (HB 1532, signed 12 May 2026), Public Utilities 4-212(c)(1)(i), p.34 of the session law: 'On or before September 1, 2026, each investor-owned electric company and each electric cooperative shall submit to the Commission for approval a specific rate schedule for large load customers'. BGE's, Pepco's and Delmarva's filings were not read: the PSC's docket system (webpscxb.psc.state.md.us) bars Claude's agents in its robots file (refused). A lead: HB 1082 of 2026 would have moved that date to 1 January 2027 (its fiscal note); Chapter 353 as enacted keeps 1 September 2026. Exelon's Q3 2026 earnings slides (SEC EDGAR, exc-20261030ex992.htm, p.1) give a combined MidAtlantic figure: 'MidAtlantic ~2 GW' of high probability load and 'MidAtlantic ~9 GW' within cluster studies (MidAtlantic covers PECO, BGE, Pepco, Delmarva and Atlantic City Electric). Status updated by the 90-day pass (east-02): was 'proposed' (2026-06-26); The adopted COMAR 20.96.01 took effect on 28 September 2026, the effective date printed in the notice of final action.

min_demand.v: no minimum bill in the policy; the refund of Eligible Dollars through annual Demand Credits over 120 months is full only when average annual billed demand is at least 90 percent of Anticipated Demand, otherwise prorated; a monthly Capacity Reservation Fee, where it applies, is 70 percent of the applicable large-load (or transmission) demand charge on the reserved demand above 2.5 MVA The Capacity Reservation Fee formula subtracts the greater of 2.5 MVA and the Available Capacity (the existing usable capacity of the system component before the upgrade); the formula itself is printed in math glyphs the text layer does not render as words.
min_demand.cite: p. 26, Appendix C: "If average annual billed demand is at least 90% of Anticipated Demand, the maximum annual credit is applied; otherwise, the credit is prorated." | p. 26, Appendix C: "returned to eligible customers through an annual Demand Credit applied once per year over 120 months (Credit Period)." | p. 25, Appendix B: "70% of the Demand Charge in the applicable large load rate schedule for customers taking delivery at primary or secondary voltage" | p. 24, Appendix A: "Available Capacity = existing usable capacity available on the relevant system component prior to the upgrade"

rules.title: CPUC Decision 25-07-039 (24 July 2025, issued 28 July 2025), Decision Partly Granting and Partly Denying Pacific Gas and Electric Company's Motion for Interim Implementation of Electric Rule Number 30, A.24-11-007
rules.clause: p. 51, Ordering Paragraph 1: "motion for interim implementation of Electric Rule 30 for large transmission-level customers (50-230 kilovolts) seeking retail service is granted in part and denied in part"
rules.basis: every value is cited to the CPUC's own docket copies (Decision 25-07-039 and the ALJ ruling of 7 August 2026, docs.cpuc.ca.gov, no robots file) or to PG&E Corporation's Form 8-K exhibit on sec.gov; nothing is cited to pge.com, whose terms bar use in publications without consent
rules.notes: The Rule 30 sheets on pge.com (Advice 7772-E, Sheets 1 to 22; internal, PG&E's terms bar use in publications without consent) print what D.25-07-039 does not: an Advance based on the Project Specific Cost Estimate (C.2), PG&E keeping the earned part of advances if the Applicant terminates before the facilities go into service (C.7), forfeiture of refunds if no service is taken by the end of the first calendar year after in-service (C.8), and Excess Facilities removal costs if load falls significantly below the Usage Forecast (C.9); no CPUC host copy of the sheets or of Advice 7772-E was found, so these stay out of the fields. Final Rule 30 still pending in A.24-11-007 on 13 November 2026: the ALJ ruling of 7 August 2026 reopened the record for comments on FERC's show cause order (EL26-71), reply comments due 4 September 2026, after which the record is submitted; no proposed or final decision was found. A partial settlement of 7 May 2026 (PG&E, Cal Advocates, CalCCA, Sierra Club) covers information sharing only (per AReM and Shell's comments, docs.cpuc.ca.gov/PublishedDocs/Efile/G000/M608/K211/608211962.PDF). Customer-specific transmission-level agreements are approved by resolution: draft Resolution E-5455 of 16 July 2026 (Google, 250 MW at 230 kV, San Jose; docs.cpuc.ca.gov/PublishedDocs/Published/G000/M607/K718/607718746.PDF) limits annual refunds to 100 percent of annual net revenues and says Resolutions E-5420, E-5433 and E-5439 limited them to 75 percent; refunds are not one of the eight fields. Refused: the CPUC proceeding page (apps.cpuc.ca.gov, robots) and PG&E's investor PDF host (s21.q4cdn.com, robots 403); the same presentation was read from the SEC copy. The pipeline counts data center load of 20 MW or more at any voltage, not only Rule 30 applicants. Status date basis: held: large_load_connection_rules/pacific_gas_and_electric_electric_rule_30.yaml (the compliance sheets of Advice 7772-E, document_date 2025-12-04); the CPUC documents read give the decision's date and its effect until the final decision, not the sheets' date Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-26): the status date was '2025-12-04', which no cited document prints (it is the Rule 30 sheets' own date, held by the ERW's registry of filed schedules, read on pge.com).

threshold_mw.v: 75 MW: a large load customer not energized by 8 October 2026 that seeks a new interconnection at a single site of 75 MW or more, an expansion reaching 75 MW for the first time, an expansion of a site over 75 MW by 75 MW or more, or co-location with a generation resource; at transmission or distribution voltage; for an expansion the rule applies to the added load
threshold_mw.cite: p. 25, §25.194(b)(1): "(b) Applicability. (1) This section applies to a large load customer that has not energized as of the effective date ofthis section and that seeks: (A) a new interconnection at a single site that is equal to or exceeds 75 megawatts (MW); (B) an expanded interconnection at a single site that equals or exceeds 75 MW for the first time; or (C) an expanded interconnection at a single site that exceeds 75 MW and is expanding by 75 MW or more; or (D) to co-locate with a generation resource." | p. 28, §25.194(c)(14): "(14) Large load customer -- An entity requesting a new or expanded interconnection where the customer's total expected non-coincident peak demand at a single site is equal to or exceeds 75 MW, whether at transmission voltage or distribution voltage."

collateral.v: intermediate agreement: $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand (or of the incremental increase), posted at execution; SLLIA: the greater of $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand or the system upgrade costs allocated by the (batch zero) interconnection study, posted at SLLIA execution, plus possible additional security for the minimum billing demand; accepted forms: cash in a segregated interest-bearing account, a guaranty from a guarantor rated at least BBB- (S&P), Baa3 (Moody's) or BBB- (Fitch), or a letter of credit from a bank rated at least A-, A3 or A-; the $50,000 adjusted by CPI every five years from 2032; direct interconnection costs paid as non-refundable cash CIAC with no allowance
collateral.cite: p. 36, §25.194(d)(2)(B): "A large load customer must post financial security with the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP in the amount of $50,000 per MW of the requested peak demand for new interconnection requests or $50,000 per MW of the incremental increase in the peak demand for expanded interconnection requests." | p. 52, §25.194(f)(2)(B)(i): "A large load customer must post financial security with the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP in an amount that is the greater of: (I) $50,000 per MW ofthe contracted peak demand; or" | p. 53, §25.194(f)(2)(B)(i)(II): "the costs allocated to the large load customer for system upgrades as a result of a batch zero interconnection study or an interconnection study." | p. 53, §25.194(f)(2)(B)(iii): "Financial security under this subsection must be posted at the time the SLLIA is executed." | p. 37, §25.194(d)(2)(B)(ii): "(I) cash collateral to be held in a segregated, cash account bearing interest at a rate equal to at least the rate of the constant maturity one-month U.S. Treasury bill" | p. 37, §25.194(d)(2)(B)(ii): "guaranty, only if the guarantor has a U.S. or international credit rating of at least "BBB-" from Standard & Poor's, "Baa3" from Moody's Investor Service, or "BBB-" from Fitch." | p. 38, §25.194(d)(2)(B)(ii): "a letter of credit issued by a major U.S. commercial bank, or a U.S. branch office of a major foreign commercial bank, with a U.S. or international credit rating of at least "A-" from Standard & Poor's, "A3" from Moody's Investor Service, or "A-" from Fitch." | p. 37, §25.194(d)(2)(B)(i): "Beginning in 2032, the commission will adjust the $50,000 value on January 1 every five years in accordance with this clause." | p. 55, §25.194(f)(2)(C): "A large load customer must pay all direct interconnection costs through CIAC, with no standard or other allowance offered to offset the customer's CIAC payments. (i) CIAC must be paid in the form of a direct cash payment." | p. 55, §25.194(f)(2)(C): "(v) CIAC is not refundable."

exit_fee.v: outstanding amounts owed are paid first (costs incurred, non-cancellable equipment, construction and services, and after a SLLIA the minimum billing demand for its set period); withdrawal before the study, or after a zero-MW allocation: full return of the rest; withdrawal after a partial allocation but before the SLLIA deadline: 20% of the security for the allocated capacity kept (50% for batch zero loads under Planning Guide 9.2.1.1(1)(f)); no SLLIA by the deadline: security forfeited; withdrawal of contracted demand after a SLLIA: 20% of the security for the withdrawn demand kept; energization schedule missed by 24 months: security drawn for amounts owed and 20% of the security for the non-utilized capacity kept; CIAC not refundable
exit_fee.cite: p. 40, §25.194(d)(3)(A)(iii): "(II) costs for equipment that the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP procured and that cannot be canceled or returned with a full refund;" | p. 57, §25.194(f)(3)(A): "(V) the large load minimum billing demand described in §25.193 of this title for the set period oftime described in §25.193." | p. 40, §25.194(d)(3)(B): "(i) the large load customer withdraws its requests for interconnection before ERCOT begins the interconnection study; or (ii) the large load customer is included in an interconnection study, is allocated zero MW across all study years by ERCOT, and withdraws" | p. 41, §25.194(d)(3)(C): "the interconnecting DSP or interconnecting TSP must subtract 20% of the financial security associated with the transmission capacity allocated by ERCOT to a large load customer that is included in an interconnection study, is allocated some portion of its requested peak demand, and withdraws its interconnection request before the deadline to execute a SLLIA" | p. 42, §25.194(d)(3)(E): "is deemed to have forfeited any financial security that the large load customer posted under an intermediate agreement." | p. 57, §25.194(f)(3)(B): "subtract 20% of the financial security associated with the contracted peak demand that is withdrawn before the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP returns the remaining balance of financial security posted by a large load customer." | p. 60, §25.194(g)(3): "must subtract 20% of the financial security associated with the non-utilized transmission capacity and then return the balance to the large load customer." | p. 63, §25.194(h)(1)(C): "(i) 50% of the financial security associated with the transmission capacity allocated by ERCOT to a large load customer that meets the criteria in ERCOT Planning Guide Section 9.2.1.1(1)(f)"

rules.title: PUCT Project No. 58481, Order Adopting New 16 TAC §25.194 (filed 18 September 2026, item 218), third of three files (adoption order pages 200 to 270: the rule text and the ordering paragraph)
rules.clause: p. 25, §25.194(a): "§25.194. Large Load Interconnection Standards. (a) Purpose and Scope. This section sets forth the standards and criteria for an electric utility,"
rules.basis: the PUCT's own docket copy (interchange.puc.texas.gov, Project 58481, items 218 and 219)
rules.notes: Status: adopted by the order filed 18 September 2026 (the signature date on page 71 is illegible in the scan); effective 8 October 2026 per the Texas Register's acknowledgment (issue of 2 October 2026, TRD 202604027) The rule binds electric utilities, municipally owned utilities and electric cooperatives interconnecting large loads to the ERCOT system (subsection (a)); a municipally owned utility or cooperative may add its own requirements: 'Nothing in this section limits the authority of a municipally owned utility or an electric cooperative to impose electric service requirements for large load customers on their systems in addition to the standards adopted under this section' (page 25). Also in the rule, not entered as fields: required disclosures under both agreements (site control with a lease of at least five years, substantially similar requests elsewhere in Texas, water, backup generation, power supply, controllable load resource), audit and verification by ERCOT and commission staff with forfeiture and reallocation for false information (subsections (j), (k)), and the transition for customers that signed a §25.370(g) agreement (subsection (i)). A batch zero load with an interconnection agreement signed on or before 1 June 2025 pays direct interconnection costs under that agreement (subsection (h)(3)(B), page 65). The Texas Register's own pages were not read (sos.state.tx.us answered 403 on the October 9 issue; the adoption was submitted for the issue of 2 October 2026).

collateral.v: 16 TAC §25.194: $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand at the intermediate agreement; the greater of $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand or allocated system upgrade costs at the SLLIA; cash collateral held in a segregated interest-bearing account; direct interconnection costs as cash CIAC; AEP Texas segregated about $1.2 billion of cash collateral in October 2026 and received about $2 billion of Batch Zero security in July 2026 as cash, corporate or parental guarantees and letters of credit; the accepted forms besides cash collateral are a guaranty (guarantor rated at least BBB- or Baa3) or a letter of credit from a major bank rated at least A- or A3
collateral.cite: https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 36, §25.194(d)(2)(B): "A large load customer must post financial security with the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP in the amount of $50,000 per MW of the requested peak demand for new interconnection requests or $50,000 per MW of the incremental increase in the peak demand for expanded interconnection requests." | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 52, §25.194(f)(2)(B)(i): "A large load customer must post financial security with the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP in an amount that is the greater of: (I) $50,000 per MW ofthe contracted peak demand; or" | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 37, §25.194(d)(2)(B)(ii): "(I) cash collateral to be held in a segregated, cash account bearing interest at a rate equal to at least the rate of the constant maturity one-month U.S. Treasury bill" | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 55, §25.194(f)(2)(C): "A large load customer must pay all direct interconnection costs through CIAC, with no standard or other allowance offered to offset the customer's CIAC payments. (i) CIAC must be paid in the form of a direct cash payment." | Large Load Interconnections in Texas: "requires utilities to segregate cash collateral posted as financial security. In October 2026, AEP Texas segregated approximately $1.2 billion of cash collateral pursuant to the new rule." | Large Load Interconnections in Texas: "In July 2026, AEP Texas received approximately $2 billion of financial security in the form of cash collateral, corporate or parental guarantees and letters of credit" | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 37, 16 TAC 25.194(d)(2)(B)(ii): "guaranty, only if the guarantor has a U.S. or international credit rating of at least "BBB-" from Standard & Poor's" | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 38, 16 TAC 25.194(d)(2)(B)(ii): "a letter of credit issued by a major U.S. commercial bank"

exit_fee.v: 16 TAC §25.194: 20% of the security for allocated capacity kept on withdrawal before the SLLIA deadline, 20% of the security for withdrawn contracted demand kept after a SLLIA, a customer that neither withdraws before the SLLIA deadline nor executes a SLLIA forfeits the security posted under its intermediate agreement; CIAC not refundable (statewide row)
exit_fee.cite: https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 41, §25.194(d)(3)(C): "the interconnecting DSP or interconnecting TSP must subtract 20% of the financial security associated with the transmission capacity allocated by ERCOT to a large load customer that is included in an interconnection study, is allocated some portion of its requested peak demand, and withdraws its interconnection request before the deadline to execute a SLLIA" | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 57, §25.194(f)(3)(B): "subtract 20% of the financial security associated with the contracted peak demand that is withdrawn before the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP returns the remaining balance of financial security posted by a large load customer." | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 41-42, 16 TAC 25.194(d)(3)(E): "A large load customer that does not withdraw its interconnection request before the deadline to execute a SLLIA and does not execute a SLLIA before the deadline ... is deemed to have forfeited any financial security that the large load customer posted under an intermediate agreement" | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 55, 16 TAC 25.194(f)(2)(C)(v): "CIAC is not refundable."

study_timeline.v: 16 TAC §25.194: $100,000 study fee; the TSP or DSP contacts ERCOT within 60 days after the intermediate agreement is executed and funded and tells the customer within five working days; AEP's 10-Q reports ERCOT's Batch Zero study paused (notes)
study_timeline.cite: https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 35, §25.194(d)(2)(A): "(i) A large load customer must pay a study fee of $100,000 to the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP for transmission studies performed by the interconnecting DSP, the interconnecting TSP, and ERCOT, as applicable." | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 43, §25.194(e)(1): "Not later than 60 days after an intennediate agreement is executed and funded under subsection (d) of this section, the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must contact ERCOT to initiate an interconnection study, as prescribed by ERCOT protocols." | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 44, §25.194(e)(2)(A): "The interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must notify the large load customer not later than five working days after the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP contacts ERCOT to initiate an interconnection study."

connection_timeline.v: 16 TAC §25.194: SLLIA within 60 days after ERCOT's study report; capacity reported as non-utilized if the energization schedule is missed by 24 months; AEP's 10-Q: ERCOT will not authorize large loads to energize until its verification is complete (notes)
connection_timeline.cite: https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 45, §25.194(f): "Not later than 60 days after ERCOT issues a study report that allocates transmission capacity, the large load customer must execute and fund a SLLIA with the interconnecting DSP and, if different from the interconnecting DSP, the interconnecting TSP." | https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/58481_218_1684656.PDF (read 2026-11-13) p. 59, §25.194(g)(1): "Not later than 30 days after a large load customer fails, by 24 months, to satisfy a milestone in its schedule for phased energization, as described in the SLLIA at the time of execution, the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must notify ERCOT of the large load customer's non-utilized capacity."

rules.title: City of Austin, Recommendation for Action, File 26-1045, Agenda Item 8, 26 February 2026 (Austin Energy): repeal of City Code Section 15-9-5
rules.clause: p. 1: "Repealing this Code provision ensures consistency with current policy and allows Austin Energy to require 100 percent cost recovery."
rules.basis: City of Austin public records (services.austintexas.gov: council backup, ordinance, Austin Energy presentation)
rules.notes: Status: the full-cost-recovery policy itself dates from Resolution 20140612-057 (2014); the ordinance removed the older partial-recovery code section The February 2026 presentation calls the repealed section the '2003 City Code'; the ordinance and the RCA say Section 15-9-5 was adopted in 2004. The Electric Utility Commission recommended the repeal on 9 February 2026 (8-0). City work session transcript (https://services.austintexas.gov/edims/document.cfm?id=480040, page 7): 'Austin energy currently serves ten data centers. These facilities, for the most part, are 20mw and under. At this time, Austin energy is not aware of any interconnection requests' for a hyperscale data center (a caption transcript, so not entered as a queue value). Council was to take up a data center resolution (item 61, 27 August 2026) to begin code amendments; its outcome was not read. 16 TAC §25.194 (statewide row, in effect 8 October 2026) also binds municipally owned utilities interconnecting loads of 75 MW or more to the ERCOT system, and leaves them free to add requirements of their own (its subsection (a)).

min_demand.v: On-peak billing demand (and likewise off-peak) not less than a stepped share of the higher of contract demand or the highest billing demand of the preceding 12 months: 30 percent of the first 5,000 kW, 40 percent of the next 20,000 kW, 50 percent of the next 25,000 kW, 60 percent of the next 50,000 kW, 70 percent of the next 100,000 kW, 80 percent of the next 150,000 kW and 85 percent of all kW above 350,000 kW. For contract demand over 5,000 kW, off-peak energy billed at not less than 110 hours (15 percent load factor) of off-peak billing demand. Minimum monthly bill of the service, administrative, demand and energy charges; the Division may require higher minimum bills. TVA reviews the preceding 36 months and adjusts the contract if billing demand is below 75 percent of contract demand
min_demand.cite: p. 2, Determination of On-peak and Off-peak Demands: "The on-peak billing demand shall in no case be less than the sum of (1) 30 percent of the first 5,000 kW, (2) 40 percent of the next 20,000 kW, (3) 50 percent of the next 25,000 kW, (4) 60 percent of the next 50,000 kW, (5) 70 percent of the next 100,000 kW, (6) 80 percent of the next 150,000 kW, and (7) 85 percent of all kW in excess of 350,000 kW of the higher of the currently effective on-peak contract demand or the highest onpeak billing demand established during the preceding 12 months." | p. 2, Determination of On-peak and Off-peak Demands: "the off-peak energy for any month shall in no case be less than the product of (1) the off-peak billing demand as calculated in the paragraph below and (2) 110 hours (reflecting a 15 percent load factor applied to the average number of hours in a month)" | p. 3, Minimum Monthly Bill: "The Division may require minimum bills higher than those stated above." | p. 1, Availability: "If the customer's on-peak and/or off-peak billing demand is below 75% of the on-peak or off-peak contract demand, whichever is higher, an adjustment to the customer’s contract will be made."

contract_term.cite: p. 3, Contract Requirement: "Under TDCA, the contract shall be for an initial term of at least 1 year and extended automatically from year to year thereafter. After 10 years of service, any such contract for the renewal or extension of service may provide for termination upon not less than a 16-month notice."

rules.title: Memphis Light, Gas and Water Division, City of Memphis, Electric Service Schedule TDC, Time of Use Data Service (Rate effective October 1, 2026), 4 pages
rules.clause: p. 1, Availability: "This schedule shall apply to the firm electric power requirements of a customer where the major use of electricity is for activities conducted at the delivery point serving that customer which are ... used, in Tennessee Valley Authority’s (TVA) sole judgment, for the operation of computational equipment."

Leads, unverified: 256today.com (August 2026) reports the TVA Board approved a separate data center rate class at its 20 August 2026 meeting in Memphis, effective 1 October 2026 for new and existing facilities and phased in over three fiscal years, with four classes by contract demand and a capacity commitment charge of about 1.5 million USD per MW, paid over three to five years, for new or expanding data centers above 5 MW; other news reports a revised TVA Board policy for new loads above 100 MW. None of this could be read in a TVA document: tva.com and tva.gov answered robots 403, TVA's investor CDN s205.q4cdn.com (the 20 August 2026 Board press release) answered robots 403. TVA's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 notes that MLGW's contract with TVA has a five-year termination notice period. Base rates for TDCD at transmission voltage (115 kV and up), summer: on-peak billing demand 14.15 USD per kW, maximum billing demand 2.42 USD per kW (p. 4).

min_demand.v: Monthly billing demand for the Maximum Load Charge is the greatest of the month's maximum measured load, the highest measured load in the preceding 11 months, or 80 percent of contract capacity. Load ramp and load ramp period are set in each Electric Service Agreement; monthly billing begins 30 days after the customer's stated start date whether or not electricity is being provided

contract_term.v: Initial Contract Term of not less than 15 years; either party gives at least 60 months' advance written notice to discontinue (the notice does not shorten the initial term except through the Exit Fee); contract capacity may be reduced only after the first 5 years of the initial term, on 60 months' written notice and with a Capacity Reduction Fee
contract_term.cite: p. 36, Sheet No. 26.1, Term of Contract: "Contracts under this rate schedule shall be made for an Initial Contract Term of not less than fifteen (15) years." | p. 36, Sheet No. 26.1, Term of Contract: "Either party shall give at least 60 months advance written notice to the other party of its intention to discontinue service under the terms of this rate schedule. collateral.v: Cash or letter of credit equal to 24 months of minimum billed amounts at the largest contract capacity; 12 months if the customer or its guarantor is rated at least A (S&P) and A2 (Moody's) and holds cash and cash equivalents of at least 10 times the requirement. Due at signing of the Electric Service Agreement; an increased requirement after an adverse credit change is due within three business days of written notice. Letter of credit from a bank with assets of at least 10 billion USD rated at least A- and A3
collateral.cite: p. 37, Sheet No. 26.2, Collateral Requirements: "Customer or its guarantor shall provide collateral in the form of cash or Letter of Credit equal to 24 months of the minimum billed amounts at the largest contract capacity value." | p. 37, Sheet No. 26.2, Collateral Requirements: "If Customer or its guarantor has an S&P Credit Rating of at least A and a Moody’s Credit Rating of at least A2 with cash and cash equivalents on its audited balance sheet of at least 10 times the collateral requirement, Customer or its guarantor shall provide cash or a Letter of Credit equal to 12 months of the annual minimum billed amounts at the largest contract capacity value." | p. 37, Sheet No. 26.2, Collateral Requirements: "The collateral requirement is due at the signing of the Electric Service Agreement. If Company becomes aware of an adverse change to Customer’s or its guarantor’s creditworthiness, Customer or its guarantor shall provide Company the increased collateral requirement due within three business days after written notice."

rules.title: Minnesota Statutes 2026, section 216B.1622, SERVICE TO VERY LARGE CUSTOMERS (Office of the Revisor of Statutes)
rules.clause: p. 1, Subd. 2: "The commission may approve, modify, or reject a tariff or electric service agreement proposed between a public utility and a very large customer establishing the terms and conditions under which the utility will provide electric service to the customer."
rules.basis: the State's official publication of its statutes and session laws
rules.notes: Required outcomes the Commission must consider (subd. 2): costs of very large customers assigned to their class; electricity meeting the § 216B.1691 benchmarks; protections so other customers are not placed at risk for stranded costs. Subd. 3: the section does not apply to existing, renewed or extended ESAs or to very large customers taking service before 2020. Related definition (Minn. Stat. § 216B.02, subd. 11, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216B.02): a data center is a facility designed to have a load of 100 megawatts or more. The MPUC's data center page (https://mn.gov/puc/activities/v-l-e-c/data-centers/) names §§ 216B.1622 and 216B.1623 and an annual ECO fund fee of 2 to 5 million dollars for qualified large-scale data centers (not a connection term). Status date as the reading group wrote it: '2025-06-14 (signed; the section is effective the day following final enactment)'. Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-29): the status date was '2025-06-14', the governor's signature; the act takes effect 'the day following final enactment', a date the text does not print.

changes.rule: Tentative Order proposing amendments to 52 Pa. Code 57.51 to 57.54 (M-2026-3064961), as clarified: emergency curtailment of large computational loads, threshold 50 MW
changes.what: After FERC rejected PJM's IRAS proposal on 9 October 2026, the PUC's Clarification Order dropped the IRAS pre-emergency curtailment proposal, kept the proposal that EDCs not classify any large load as critical load exempt from emergency curtailment, and changed the Computational Load Site threshold in the modified Appendix to a cumulative peak load of at least 50 MW at a single site within a one-mile radius; comments due 20 days after publication in the Pennsylvania Bulletin, replies 30 days. The Tentative Order had been published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin on 17 October 2026.

changes.rule: Alabama PSC generic proceeding on contracts between Alabama Power and large load data center customers (Docket 33709)

The bill's own text was not read (the release, not the enrolled act, is the source).

laws.requirements: cost allocation: The Public Utility Commission provides a separate classification of service with its own tariff schedule for large energy use facilities; the tariff allocates the class's costs to the class, or directly assigns a facility's costs to it, and mitigates the risk of shifting costs to other classes [p. 1, Section 2(2): "The Public Utility Commission shall provide for a classification of service under ORS 757.230 for retail electricity consumers that are large energy use facilities." | p. 1, Section 2(2)(a)(A): "Allocate the costs of serving the class of retail electricity consumers that are large energy use facilities to the class in a manner that is equal or proportional to the costs of serving the class"] || minimum term: The contract with a large energy use facility is for 10 years or longer [p. 1, Section 5(1)(b)(A)(ii): "Specify the duration of the contract and be for a duration for 10 years or longer"] || minimum bill: The contract obligates the customer to pay a minimum amount or percentage, set by the commission, based on its projected electricity usage, for the contract's duration [p. 1, Section 5(1)(b)(A)(iv): "Obligate the retail electricity consumer to pay a minimum amount or percentage, as determined by the commission"] || other: The contract may include a charge for excess demand in addition to the tariff schedule [p. 2, Section 5(1)(b)(B): "May include a charge for excess demand for the electricity services the electric company is contracted to provide"] || disclosure: The commission reports by September 1 of each even-numbered year on load trends from large energy use facilities (repealed January 2, 2035) [p. 2, Section 7: "No later than September 1 of each even-numbered year, the Public Utility Commission shall submit a report"]

laws.bill: H. 3309 (Act No. 41 of 2025, South Carolina Energy Security Act)
laws.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE SOUTH CAROLINA CODE OF LAWS BY ENACTING THE "SOUTH CAROLINA ENERGY SECURITY ACT"
laws.status_cite: p. 1, summary: "Governor's Action: May 12, 2025, Signed" | p. 1, history: "Effective date 05/12/25" | p. 1, history: "Act No. 41" | p. 1, text: "(A41, R60, H3309)"
laws.threshold: 50 MW at one point of delivery for a 'transformational customer' (with 500 new employees, $100,000,000 investment and a Department of Commerce designation); an existing customer above 20 MW contract demand signing a contract of five years or more is a 'qualifying customer'
laws.threshold_cite: p. 1, Section 58-43-10(8)(a): "(a) 50 megawatts at one point of delivery;" | p. 1, Section 58-43-10(5)(a): "an existing commercial or industrial customer with a combined firm and interruptible contract demand greater than 20 megawatts that agrees to a new or extended electric service contract with a term of five years or more"
laws.requirements: minimum term: Economic development agreements with qualifying or transformational customers are for a term not exceeding ten years [p. 1, Section 58-43-20(C): "The agreement with the customer must be for a term not exceeding ten years"] || cost allocation: Rates for transformational customers may not be lower than 25 percent below the utility's marginal cost (qualifying customers: not below marginal cost); the commission finds measures were taken to avoid cross-customer class subsidization, and decides within sixty days [p. 1, Section 58-43-20(C): "rates for transformational customers may not be lower than twenty-five percent less than the electrical utility's marginal cost of providing service to the customer" | p. 1, Section 58-43-20(D)(2)(c): "measures have been taken to avoid or reduce cross-customer class-subsidization" | p. 1, Section 58-43-20(D): "The commission must either approve or deny an application pursuant to this section within sixty days."] || exit fee: A qualifying or transformational customer that leaves the state or ends operations during the ten-year contract reimburses the difference between standard rates and the rates it paid [p. 1, Section 58-43-20(H): "such customer must reimburse the electrical utility and its customers the difference between standard rates and the rates paid during the term of the agreement"]
laws.doc: H 3309, 126th Session (2025-2026), bill page with history and ratified text (A41, R60, H3309)

laws.title: An Act to protect residents from increased utility costs and utility shortages caused by data centers and clarify authority to regulate data centers.
laws.status_cite: p. 1, heading: "Senate Bill 135 ENROLLED"

laws.requirements: cost allocation: every provider of electricity must keep separate terms and conditions for data centers requiring them to reimburse all costs fairly attributed to them, including costs incurred to serve them if they depart the system or materially reduce load [p. 1, Section 3: "A provider of electricity shall establish and maintain separate terms and conditions for electric service applicable to a data center." | p. 1, Section 3: "including costs incurred to serve the data center if the data center departs the system or materially reduces its load."] || siting or tax: the state may not preempt or limit counties, municipalities or other subdivisions from regulating the construction, development or operation of data centers [p. 1, Section 4: "The state may not preempt or otherwise limit the authority of the governing body of a county, municipality, or other political subdivision to adopt ordinances and resolutions limiting, prohibiting, or otherwise regulating the construction, development, or operation of data centers."]

laws.status_cite: https://legislature.vermont.gov/bill/status/2026/H.727 (read 2026-11-14) p. 1, Last Recorded Action: "5/29/2026 - Veto of the Governor sustained by a vote of Yeas = 83, Nays = 52" | https://legislature.vermont.gov/Documents/2026/Docs/BILLS/H-0727/H-0727%20Vetoed%20Bill%20Summary.pdf (read 2026-11-14) p. 1, summary: "This summary is of a bill that was vetoed by the Governor" | p. 1, heading: "BILL AS PASSED BY THE HOUSE AND SENATE 2026"

laws.requirements: cost allocation: a data center would be served under a PUC-approved large load service equity contract with costs allocated equal or proportional to the cost of serving it and mitigating the risk of other classes paying unwarranted costs [p. 12, 30 V.S.A. 284(a): "a data center shall be served by an electric company pursuant to a large load service equity contract approved by the Public Utility Commission." | p. 12, 30 V.S.A. 284(b)(1): "(1) include a method for allocating costs that is equal or proportional to"] || minimum bill: a minimum amount or percentage based on projected usage for the duration of the contract, and a charge for demand above the projection [p. 13, 30 V.S.A. 284(b)(4): "(4) obligate the data center to pay a minimum amount or percentage based on the data center's projected electricity usage for the duration of the contract"] || collateral: a collateral requirement sufficient to mitigate the risk of stranded costs [p. 13, 30 V.S.A. 284(b)(6): "(6) include a collateral requirement sufficient to mitigate the risk of stranded costs;"] || curtailment or backup generation: demand-side management measures including demand response and flexible load management [p. 13, 30 V.S.A. 284(b)(7): "(7) include provisions requiring implementation of demand-side management operational measures for the purpose of maintaining grid stability and efficiency"]
